29.3 million people live in counties with no fixed-route stop. 2.4 million of them live where no dial-a-ride is reported either.

Hover a county for details

How this is counted

Fixed-route: at least one stop on a scheduled local or regional bus, light rail, subway or commuter rail route (National Transit Map), an Amtrak station or Amtrak bus stop, or an intercity bus, rail or ferry terminal such as Greyhound or Trailways (Intermodal Passenger Connectivity Database).

Dial-a-ride: at least one agency reported demand-response service in the county to the National Transit Database for 2025. It may cover only part of the county and usually needs booking ahead. "Open to anyone" means the agency reports no rider eligibility rule; the rest are for riders who qualify, such as older adults or riders with disabilities.

Not reported isn't the same as nothing. Volunteer drivers, senior center vans and Medicaid rides mostly don't report to the NTD, and the National Transit Map only has agencies that share their schedules. School buses and airports are not counted.
